# SOP Audit & Build Plan – The Forge Belfast

## **Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member lifecycle management**: Onboarding, check-ins, pause/cancellation, win-back missing—these drive retention and churn metrics.
- **Coaching consistency & development**: No audit checklist, quality standards, or coach development roadmap—directly impacts member experience and retention.
- **Churn prevention & data**: Cancellation/pause workflows, GDPR compliance, member outcome tracking all absent—revenue leakage + legal risk.
- **Referral & milestone activation**: No referral programme or milestone achievement SOP—leaving member advocacy untapped.
- **Operational supply chain**: Order Supplies & Sundries missing—impacts class delivery and member experience (mats, towels, amenities).
- **Incident & complaint escalation**: No formal troubleshooting or incident log process—reputational/legal exposure.
- **Programme launches**: No New Quarter Program Launch SOP—inconsistent communication and class scheduling.
- **Member outcomes & goals**: 30-day goals and transformation pillars undefined—no framework to measure or communicate progress to members.

---

## **Needs updating**

- **Client onboarding (24 SOPs)**: Likely missing post-sign-up touch points (day 1 check-in, week 2 class attendance check, goal-setting call); no integration with member data privacy.
- **Coach SOPs (20)**: No link between daily tasks and quality audit standards; no escalation path for underperformance or member complaints about coaching.
- **Marketing (5 SOPs)**: No referral programme mechanics or member milestone/achievement communications—organic growth lever missing.

• **Pricing is too low vs capacity.** Your Average Revenue per Member (AR/M) has collapsed from £170.43 (December) to £120.48 (June) to £9.03 (July). July's figure is nonsensical — likely a data error or summer holiday shutdown — but June at £120.48 is 29% below December and well below September–May norm of £145–£170. Immediate action: audit membership tiers (are you discounting too heavily on new sign-ups?), implement annual price increases (3–5% is standard), and tier class access (premium classes at +£10–15/month). Protect it: survey the 122–151 active members on what's working, lock in loyalty rewards (3-month or annual paid discounts), and track churn weekly. Do not raise prices without value adds (new classes, kit, PT).

• **New revenue lines: PT and class packages are untapped.** You've grown from 85 to 151 members (+78%) since September but revenue is flat (£13.8k → £17.7k June, then collapse). # Service Menu Build for The Forge

**1. Audit what you're ACTUALLY selling first**
Before writing anything down, have your coaches list every variation they're currently offering (group classes, 1-on-1 PT, nutrition, mobility work, challenges, etc.). You'll likely find inconsistency—nail that down or your menu becomes obsolete immediately.

**2. Price anchor backwards from your best member**
Don't guess pricing. Look at who's most profitable and sticky (longest retention, highest spend). What services is she buying? Build your menu packages around *that* customer, then price competitively against Belfast's other premium gyms—but 10-15% higher since you're women-only and exclusive.

**3. Create TWO menus—different jobs**
- **Coach version**: Exact deliverables, duration, effort required (so they quote consistently and don't undersell)
- **Member version**: Benefits-focused language, outcomes, what's included/excluded (simpler, visual, social-media friendly)

**4. Make inclusion crystal clear**
Spell out what's in membership vs. add-ons (guest passes, retail, locker, showers, app access, etc.). Ambiguity kills upsells. One-pager format—members should get it in 30 seconds.

**5. Test it operationally first**
Run the menu past 3-5 coaches and 10 members for 2 weeks. They'll tell you what's missing, what's priced wrong, and what's confusing before you print or post it.

**Output: One-page coach guide + one-page member guide, live in 10 days.**

**Insights**

Your July anomaly was real but unsustainable—215 leads at £2/lead suggests either a creative winner you've since paused, a targeting loophole that got closed by Meta's algo, or a one-off audience overlap. August's correction to 75 leads at £4/lead is more honest, but you've still cracked the code: 31% close rate is strong for gym trials. The profit swing (£8 per customer) confirms the model works *if* cost-per-lead stays under £5.

July-to-August tells you the efficiency cliff isn't about creative fatigue—it's about audience saturation and algorithm retraining. You're seeing normal Meta behaviour: a winning angle gets found, scales fast, then the system serves it to progressively colder audiences. Your close rate held (29→23 sales is minimal variance), so the leads quality didn't collapse; you're just buying from further down the funnel.

**Actions**

1. **Immediately audit what changed between July and August.** Pull the exact creative assets, audience definitions, placements, and bid strategies from your July top performer. Did you pause it? Did it hit frequency cap? Did you shift budget to a new audience segment that underperformed? Isolate the single creative or audience combo that drove those 215 leads and test a fresh iteration (same hook, new video/image) against current performance. If July's angle is genuinely exhausted, you need to know that fast.
